docs.title: Welcome to ReLAX
docs.text:
This napari plugin extends the functionality of the LineageTree project by providing a comprehensive Graphical User Interface (GUI). Leveraging napari’s interactive visualization capabilities and Qt’s flexible framework, it enables users to import and explore tracking datasets, called LineageTrees directly into the Napari viewer. This project as well as LineageTree lie at the interface between graph theory and biology, thus a useful glossary was created to accomodate users who are not familiar with either of the fields

With this plugin the user has access to features like:

  • Spatial and Temporal data exploration: The user can interact with the Napari viewer and the Lineage Viewer simultaneously.

  • Node Recoloring: Recolor node colors based on lineage attributes for better insights into any dataset.

  • Unordered Tree Edit Distance Calculation: Compute pairwise distances of lineages and sublineages in datasets, to assess their similarity or dissimilarity, using Unordered Tree Edit Distance (UTED).

Here are guides available for tutorials on specific aspects of workflows available in the plugin.

This integration enhances lineage analysis by combining the powerful visualization of Napari with quantitative comparison tools in an interactive environment.

docs.title: What does this combination of LineageTree and Napari offer
docs.text:
• The Viewer: The spatial data are loaded into the napari viewer and can be interacted with.
  • Interaction with big datasets: Big datasets contain hundreds of annotations/nodes per chain/branch, the plugin offers the capability to explore large lineages on the interactive Lineage Viewer
  • No need for programming knowledge: This plugin does not require programming knowledge, thus comparing LineageTrees is accessible even for the untrained user.

This plugin consists of 2 components, one tailored for single dataset analysis and inspection and one for multiple dataset analysis:

  • Single dataset analysis:

    • Lineage Viewer - Explore and Relabel: Explore the lineages with its interactive Lineage Viewer, relabel lineages of interest.
    • Attribute recoloring: Recolor nodes on both the Lineage Viewer and the Napari standard Viewer, using the distance or precomputed attributes.
    • Distance Calculation: Calculate the unordered tree edit distance, inspect the distances on the Napari Standard Viewer and create histograms to compare lineages through their sublineages.

  • Multiple dataset analysis:

    • Manager: A manager to handle and save multiple embryos.
    • Cross Dataset Comparison: Easily calculate the unordered tree edit distance of lineages or sublineages across datasets.

docs.title: Attribute Recoloring
docs.text:
This component is mainly focused on showcasing quantitative and qualitative features of the dataset by recoloring the dataset's nodes according to their attributes or their progeny.

There are 2 sections:

  • One is for recoloring any dataset according to the number of sublineages existing in a specific timepoint
  • The other is about using precomputed features to recolor both viewers on n node level.

These two components:

docs.title: Clone based recoloring
docs.text:
Using the slider, the user can select a timepoint in the dataset and recolor the whole dataset according to the number of clones existing on this timepoint. For example if the user selects timepoint 2 in the demo C. Elegans dataset, two colors will be shown, one for each sublineage in timepoint 2.

The user can also change the colormap, by interactring with the combobox, if they prefer an other array of colors.

docs.title: Node based recoloring
docs.text:
The user can select any quantitative attribute and recolor it according to its value. Top: The configuration screen and the colored Napari viewer. Bottom: One lineage that has been recolored is shown on the Lineage Viewer.

The user may select how to handle nodes that have no value:

  1. Black: If a node has no value, no color, it will be shown in black color.
  2. Propagate from Ancestor: Each node with no value will inherit its value from its ancestor and be colored the same color.
  3. Propagate from Sibling: Each node with no value will get the same value as their sibling if they do have a color.
  4. Default Value: More settings are available here, as the user can select a value to color each node that has no color.
    1. Custom Value: The user can input any value, so these nodes will get this value.
    2. Mean: Each node will be colored with the mean value.
    3. Median: Each node will be colored with the median value.
    4. Min: Each node will be colored with the minimum value.

Go to Starting page Go to Tutorials

docs.title: Distance Calculation
docs.text:
For comparisons across embryos the User Interface remains as close as possible to Distance Calculation. However some changes have been made to accomodate the needs of such an analysis.

  1. Tree approximation selection: Similar to Distance Calculation, however any differences in time resolution are handled automatically by the manager.

  2. Dataset Selection: The user may select as many datasets from the manager as they want. Each selected dataset is added as a tab on 3

  3. Configuring the roots: This component is identical to Distance Calculation. An Important thing is that the user has to decide the levels of comparison and the crop times independently, so these comparisons need some prior rough analysis using the populations of cells of an embryo.

  1. Tree graphs: The lineages that are currently being compared.

  2. The cusltermap: The clustermap that contains all the roots that are being compared and it's configuration/save buttons.

  3. The 2 dummy viewers: These viewers work independent to each other so the user may inspect different timepoints and different angles in each dataset. In this specific image the El lineage of 2 Parhyale hawaiensis embryos is being compared

The histogram has not been implemented yet for cross comparison, but it is in the works.

docs.title: Manager
docs.text: When comparing multiple datasets, users must account for various parameters, one of the most critical being temporal resolution. Recent advances in imaging and acquisition techniques have enabled significantly improved time resolution, leading to increased adoption of these modern tools. Consequently, integrating or comparing legacy datasets with newer, high-resolution data has become challenging. This component is designed specifically to address this issue by managing differences in temporal resolution, thereby allowing users to concentrate on the analysis and interpretation of the data rather than on preprocessing or alignment tasks.

docs.title: Manager
docs.text:
1. Create a Manager from existing layers: Pressing this button will create a new manager that consists of all the layers of napari that contain a LineageTree.
  2. Load an existing Manager
  3. The LineageTree list: This list contains all the LineageTrees the current manager contains. Users may interact with this list with right-click to change the time resolutions of any dataset or remove it.
  4. Add a LineageTree from the manager to the viewer: Add a LineageTree from the manager to the viewer if it does not already exist in the layer list.
  5. Add an embryo from file: Imports an embryo from a file directly to the viewer.
  6. Save the Manager: Save the manager.

docs.title: Distance Calculation
docs.text:
Distance Calculation focuses on systematic calculation of unordered tree edit distances of lineaeges and their sublineages across multiple timepoints, using various approximation methods.

This systematic comparison enables users to calculate the pairwise distance of clones/sublineages that spawn from a specific timepoint, across multiple timepoints.

The results of these comparisons will be shown on a clustermap, which the user can download. However, a clustermap by itself is lacking in information, or at least is difficult to interpret the results in means of morphology, for this reason we allow for users to click on this clustermap to inspect which sublineages are being compared in each specific cell!

docs.title: Configuration Tab
docs.text:
This Tab is responsible for setting up the systematic pairwise distance parameters.

  1. Timepoints Selection: The user has two options to set the timepoints for the comparison:
    • Top: The user may set a range with steps.
    • Bottom: The user may set a list of specific timepoints they want to compare.
  2. Time crop: The last timepoint to be included in the analysis. If the tree has nodes at later timepoints, they will be excluded (cut) from the analysis.
  3. Approximation / Style selection: The approximation to be used in the analysis. CAUTION: Different algorithms have different uses. For more information, visit LineageTree Tree approximations . The full tree mode is not recommended for large LineageTrees.
  4. Subtree selection: Specific lineages may be selected to calculate their pairwise distances. Some lineages may spawn later than the first selected timepoint due to tracking or imaging issues; they can still be included if they exist at any of the selected timepoints.
  5. Start / Stop Comparisons: The user can start calculating the comparisons. While the comparisons are being processed, the rest of the plugin and Napari remain responsive. At any point, the user may stop processing by clicking Stop Processing. A progress bar indicates the calculation progress.

docs.title: Clustermap Tab
docs.text:
Using this component the user can calculate the unordered tree edit distance for any lineage or sublineage and the sublineages spawned by their ancestors.

  1. Tree plots: Displays the trees that are currently being interacted with through the clustermap, with their subtrees colored according to the colors of the viewer.
  2. Clustermap Configuration: Using the left combobox, the user may select their preferred normalization method according to the analysis they wish to perform. The right combobox allows the user to choose different color gradients for recoloring the clustermap.
  3. Clustermap: The clustermap is generated through systematic comparisons. There is one clustermap for each timepoint selected in the configuration component. This clustermap is normalized by 2.
    • Interaction is performed by Left Click on any element in the plot, which creates the corresponding tree graphs and recolors the selected embryo according to the compared sublineages.

Go to Starting page Go to Tutorials

docs.title: Explore and Relabel
docs.text: This component focuses on interacting with chain-level temporal data rather than node-level data. This approach makes plotting and analyzing lineages faster and more efficient. It is the first tab of the Lineage tree analysis widget (Plugins>Lineage tree analysis).

docs.title: Core Features
docs.text:
The main capabilities of this component include:

  • Explore temporal data efficiently using the Lineage Viewer.
  • Relabel any chain in a LineageTree dataset.
  • Combination of the Lineage Viewer with the Napari Viewer for easy exploration of both temporal and spatial data.
  • Iterate through all lineages existing in a dataset using a slider, or jump to any cell using its ID.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text:
Screenshot from an earlier version

Since this screenshot was taken, the configuration button and window (1 and 2) moved to napari's preferences, a Cell ID selector was added under the lineage slider (4), and a Reset slider button was added next to the size slider (8). The descriptions below match the current version.

  1. Lineage Viewer settings (1 and 2 in the screenshot): the node size, edge size and font size of the Lineage Viewer are set in napari's File>Preferences, on the ReLAX page (napari 0.9 or newer).
  2. The Lineage Viewer: Using this viewer, the user may inspect all the lineages in the dataset. The current timepoint of the Napari Viewer is drawn on it.

    Controlling the Lineage Viewer:

    • Left click: Select the sublineage spawned from the clicked node on both viewers. Clicking an empty area clears the selection and shows hidden nodes again.
    • Double Left click: Move the Napari Viewer to the first timepoint of the clicked cell.
    • Mouse wheel: Using the mouse wheel, the user can zoom in on the Lineage Viewer to observe specific details. If zoomed in enough, the labels of each node will be shown on screen.
    • Right click and drag: Pan to see different segments of the lineage if the plot is zoomed in.
    • Z: Reset the view regardless of panning or zoom.
  3. Lineage slider: Use the slider to inspect the different lineages that exist in the dataset. Its tooltip shows how many lineages are available; small lineages may be hidden by the Filter Dataset option used when opening the dataset.
    • Cell ID selector (under the slider): type a cell ID and press Enter or Go. The Lineage Viewer shows the lineage containing this cell and circles it, the cell is selected in the Napari Viewer, and the time slider moves to its first timepoint. If the ID does not exist, the closest existing ID is used.
  4. Label manipulation: The text field shows the ID and label of the current node (ID of root: … - Label: …). Type a new label and press Enter to rename it, press Remove this label to delete it, or Show Labels to list all labels. Labels are used by Distance Calculation and saved with the LineageTree.
  5. Select Lineage/Sub-Lineage: After the user has selected a point on the Napari Viewer with Shift + Right click, they may select the lineage that spawns this node (Select Lineage) or the sublineage spawned by this node (Select Sub-Lineage). This will also update the plot. The user may also decide to change the colors of all nodes selected using the layer controls.
  6. Show/Hide Lineages: Hide Lineage hides the selected lineage, Show Lineage shows only the selected lineage, and Hide all / Show all apply to every lineage. Linked mesh layers follow. Lineages that are hidden may still be selected using the Lineage Viewer.
  7. Shared tools, at the bottom of the Lineage tree analysis widget and visible in every tab:
    • Size of spheres: Change the size of the Points of the selected layer, or of all layers when All layers is ticked. Reset slider restores the size estimated from the distances between neighboring cells.
    • Toggle visibility of other layers: When ticked, selecting a layer hides all the other layers; the same result may be achieved by Alt+Click on a layer in the layer list.
    • Add Tracks: Add a tracks layer to the selected Points layer for visualization purposes.
    • Save LineageTree: Choose a file with Select file, then press Save LineageTree to save the dataset, with its labels and comparisons, as a .lT file.

docs.text:
This layer was produced by pressing on Add Tracks while a viable layer (contains a LineageTree) was selected

docs.title: Below you’ll find links to individual guides, each focusing on a specific aspect of the workflow.
📚 Tutorials Overview
docs.text: Use these guides to explore each part of the ReLAX workflow — from loading and visualizing datasets to performing complex comparisons and saving results.

docs.title: 💾 Saving Progress and Relabelling
docs.text: Learn how to preserve manual labels and pairwise distance calculations after modifying a LineageTree. Covers node selection, label editing, and saving options.

docs.title: 👁️ Managing Lineage Visibility
docs.text: Discover how to hide or show specific lineages to better visualize overlapping layers in complex 3D datasets.

docs.title: 📂 Opening a Dataset
docs.text: Step-by-step instructions on how to load datasets into ReLAX. Covers supported file formats, importing lineage data, and troubleshooting common loading issues.

docs.title: 🧬 Blind comparison of Lineages
docs.text: Learn how to perform blind comparisons across all possible lineage pairs to identify clusters of similar sublineages. Includes guidance on timepoint selection, dataset cropping, distance style configuration, and result interpretation.

docs.title: 🧬 🔬 🧬 Across-Embryo Lineage Comparison
docs.text: Explore how to compare lineages across different embryos, specimens, or even species. Learn how to align datasets, manage time resolution, configure comparison parameters, and interpret cross-dataset clustermaps.

docs.title: Opening a Dataset
docs.text: Importing data is one of the most important aspects of this plugin. All the supported formats can be easily opened using Drag and Drop onto the napari window, or with File>Open File(s).... If there is no available data, the user may use one of the sample datasets the plugin comes with: File>Open Sample>ReLAX>demo lineageTree dataset or C. elegans dataset (see Quick Start).

docs.title: 1. Check the Format
docs.text:
Format Extension Notes LineageTree .lT Native format. Also stores the labels and comparisons made in ReLAX. MaMuT or ASTEC .xml ReLAX asks which of the two tools produced the file. Mastodon .mastodon Mastodon project file. BMF .bmf

LineageTree can read more formats, for example CSV, TGMM XML or SWC files. To open one of them in ReLAX, convert it to .lT first:

from lineagetree import read_from_csv

lT = read_from_csv("tracks.csv")
lT.write("tracks.lT")

The LineageTree loaders documentation lists all readers and their options.

docs.title: 2. Choose the Loader (.xml only)
docs.text: When several loaders can read the file, a lineagetree data type selection window asks the user to select the method used to produce the dataset. Tick the tool that produced the file: MaMuT XML loader or ASTEC XML loader. Closing the window without choosing stops the import.

docs.title: 3. Set the Loading Parameters
docs.text:
Every file then opens a Loading Parameters window:

  • Time resolution (mins): the time between two consecutive timepoints, pre-filled with the value stored in the dataset. The Manager uses it to align datasets acquired at different rates.
  • Resave dataset with new time resolution: writes the dataset with the new time resolution as a .lT file. An opened .lT file is overwritten; for other formats, .lT is added to the file name (embryo.xml becomes embryo.xml.lT).
  • Rescale Dataset: divides all positions by the largest distance between two cells of the dataset, so that datasets with different spatial units appear at a similar scale.
  • Filter Dataset: hides small lineages from the Lineage Viewer. With a value n above 0, only lineages with at least (number of timepoints) / n nodes are listed; 0 keeps every lineage. All cells are still shown in the napari viewer.

Press Ok to load the dataset or Cancel to abort.

docs.title: 4. Start Exploring
docs.text:
Loading a dataset adds:

  • a Points layer named after the file, with one point per cell and timepoint, colored by lineage;
  • a Surface layer named <file name>_mesh if the dataset contains cell meshes. It is linked to the Points layer.

Select the Points layer and open Plugins>Lineage tree analysis to explore it with the Lineage Viewer.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• The file is not offered to ReLAX: check that its extension is one of the supported ones above, or convert it to .lT.
  • "Please select one reader function.": the loader window was closed without choosing a loader. Open the file again and tick one.
  • Ok does nothing in the Loading Parameters window: the time resolution must be a number.

docs.title: Blind Comparison of Lineages
docs.text: By calculating the distance between two lineages, users can identify which lineages or sublineages are similar or dissimilar. Manually selecting pairs for comparison can be tedious and time-consuming. This guide demonstrates how to automatically compare every possible pair of lineages to reveal clusters of similar lineages.

docs.title: 0. (Optional) Label the dataset:
docs.text: The imported dataset may not contain predefined labels. However, adding labels can greatly enhance the interpretation and comparison of lineages. To learn how to assign and save labels, follow the instructions in Relabelling and Saving Progress

docs.title: 1. Select Timepoints
docs.text: Define the range of timepoints from which sublineages will be analyzed. For a blind search, it is recommended to start from the beginning of the dataset and stop at a timepoint where cell divisions are still occurring.

docs.title: 2. Crop the Dataset
docs.text: Lineages result from tracking, which depends heavily on data quality. In some cases, certain lineages are tracked more accurately than others. Because UTED is sensitive to differences in tree size, unequal tracking quality can lead to unreliable results. To minimize this, crop the dataset at a timepoint where most lineages of interest are still active and have not yet stopped dividing.

docs.title: 3. Select a Distance Style
docs.text: Choose the method for distance calculation. For blind discovery of similar lineages, the full tree is highly not recommended.

docs.title: 4. Select Roots
docs.text: If you wish to compare sublineages from specific roots, select those roots by left-clicking on them. To include all roots in the analysis, select one root and press Ctrl + A to highlight them all.

docs.title: 5. Run the Comparison
docs.text: Start the process by clicking Run Comparisons. The tool will calculate distances between all possible lineage pairs within the selected parameters.

docs.title: 6. Inspect the Results
docs.text: Examine the resulting clustermap to identify potential clusters of similar lineages. Experiment with different colormaps and normalization settings to highlight meaningful patterns and refine the results.

docs.title: 7. Explore the Clustermap
docs.text: Click on an interesting cell in the clustermap (at any timepoint) to view how the corresponding sublineages contribute to the overall morphology. Repeat this step as many times as needed to explore different relationships.

docs.title: 8. (Optional) Save the Comparisons
docs.text: Save any interesting comparison results for further analysis using external data analysis tools or libraries.

docs.title: Cross-Dataset Lineage Comparison
docs.text: Comparing lineages within a single embryo can provide valuable insights into the developmental patterns of that organism. However, even more knowledge can be gained by comparing lineages across different specimens or species. This tutorial demonstrates how to perform blind lineage comparisons between organisms, using prior knowledge to extract meaningful biological relationships.

docs.title: 0. (Optional) Label the Dataset
docs.text: The imported dataset may not contain predefined labels. However, adding labels can greatly enhance the interpretation and comparison of lineages. To learn how to assign and save labels, follow the instructions in Relabelling and Saving Progress.

docs.title: 1. Create a Manager
docs.text: First, create a Manager to handle the processes required for cross-dataset comparison. To quickly create a manager from the loaded datasets, click Create Manager from Viewer.

docs.title: 2. (Optional) Check the Time Resolution
docs.text: Time resolution is an important parameter when comparing datasets. By right-clicking on any dataset, you can modify its time resolution within the viewer. This ensures that time-dependent events are properly aligned between datasets.

docs.title: 3. Select the Datasets to Compare
docs.text: Select the datasets to be compared by clicking on each preferred dataset in the viewer.

docs.title: 4. Configure the Comparison Parameters
docs.text:
Configure the comparison parameters for each dataset individually, following the same procedure described in Blindly Comparing Lineages.

Each dataset must be configured independently to ensure accurate distance measurements. For example, it was possible to compare two Parhyale hawaiensis embryos — one starting with 8 cells and another with 19 cells. The choice of starting timepoints depends on the dataset: some can be aligned easily using their population graphs, while others may require advanced techniques such as dynamic time warping. Again, using full tree for comparison is highly not recommended

docs.title: 5. Run the Comparisons
docs.text: Once configuration is complete, press Run Comparisons to begin the analysis.

docs.title: 6. Inspect the Clustermap
docs.text: The user interface is nearly identical to that of Blindly Comparing Lineages, with the addition of two dataset viewers on the left side. In the clustermap, each dataset name is clearly displayed for easier cross-reference.

docs.title: 7. Analyze the Results
docs.text: Interpreting similarities and differences across datasets can be more challenging than when comparing a single embryo’s lineages. Clusters will usually include self-to-self lineages, while the comaprisons across embryos may not be in the center of the clusters. To gain deeper insights, it is recommended to explore multiple cells in the clustermap and examine their contributions.

docs.title: 8. (Optional) Save the Comparisons
docs.text: If the results are satisfactory, save the comparisons for future reference or further analysis using external tools and libraries.

docs.title: Saving Progress in LineageTree
docs.text:
LineageTree files can be modified using the plugin. Users who have manually assigned labels to a LineageTree or performed extensive pairwise distance calculations may wish to preserve their progress to avoid data loss.

This section describes the procedure for saving progress after such modifications.

docs.title: 1. Selecting a Node
docs.text: To modify a specific node, perform Shift + Right Click on a point within the viewer, or select the desired node directly from the Lineage Viewer panel.

docs.title: 2. Editing Labels
docs.text: Enter the appropriate label in the label field and press Enter. If pairwise comparisons have been executed, the results are automatically saved within the LineageTree file, as detailed in the Pairwise Distance Tutorial.

docs.title: 3. Saving the LineageTree
docs.text: At the bottom of the widget, press Select file to choose where to save, then press Save LineageTree. The dataset is saved as a .lT file, with its labels and comparisons.

docs.title: Managing Lineage Visibility in 3D Datasets
docs.text:
Some three-dimensional (3D) datasets may contain multiple tissue layers, where one lineage obscures another and prevents clear visualization. To address this, users can temporarily hide selected lineages to reveal structures that are otherwise difficult to inspect.

In the following example, a Parhyale hawaiensis embryo has developed multiple tissue layers that overlap and hinder detailed examination.

docs.title: 1. Identifying Obstructing Lineages
docs.text: In this example, the lime and red lineages obscure the underlying layer. Begin by selecting any node belonging to the lineage that is obstructing the area of interest.

docs.title: 2. Selecting the Lineage
docs.text: Once a node is selected, click Select Lineage to highlight the entire lineage.

docs.title: 3. Hiding the Lineage
docs.text: Click Hide Lineage to conceal the selected lineage. Repeat this process for all additional lineages that need to be hidden.

docs.title: 4. Inspecting Inner Layers
docs.text: After all obstructing lineages have been hidden, the inner layers become clearly visible and can be examined in detail.

docs.title: 5. Restoring All Lineages
docs.text: Once the inspection is complete, click Show all to restore visibility to all previously hidden lineages.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
ReLAX requires Python 3.11 or newer and napari 0.9 or newer. You can install napari-relax via pip:

pip install napari-relax

If napari is not already installed, you can install napari-relax with napari and Qt via:

pip install "napari-relax[all]"

To install the latest development version:

pip install git+https://github.com/GuignardLab/napari-relax.git

docs.title: Open the plugin
docs.text:
ReLAX adds two widgets to napari's Plugins menu:

  • Lineage tree analysis: explore, relabel, recolor and compare the lineages of one dataset.
  • Cross Lineagetree comparison: compare lineages across several datasets.

docs.title: Import a dataset into the viewer
docs.text:
To import a new dataset, drag and drop a file in a supported format (.lT, MaMuT or ASTEC .xml, Mastodon or .bmf) into napari, or open it with File>Open File(s).... A short dialog then asks for the time resolution and a few loading options. See Opening a dataset for the details and for converting other formats.

There are also 2 demo datasets easily accessible from File>Open Sample>ReLAX:

  • demo lineageTree dataset contains 3 descendants of the Er lineage of Parhyale hawaiensis across the first 100 timepoints of their development. It ships with the plugin.
  • C. elegans dataset contains a C. elegans embryo starting from P0, with gene expressions from multiple experiments (from other datasets) imported. It is downloaded from Zenodo (about 42 MB) the first time it is opened, then reused.

Go to Starting page Go to Tutorials

docs.title: Napari Viewer
docs.text:
The Napari Viewer is a crucial part of this plugin, making the visualization of any tracking dataset quick and easy. Using the viewer, multiple datasets may be loaded simultaneously and can be interacted with using the viewer.

If multiple datasets are imported into napari they will usually overlap with each other, thus it's recommended to use the grid mode (Ctrl+G) to place all existing layers in a grid. The user may manually turn on/off the visibility of layers or use alt+left click on the layer of interest to hide every other layer.

docs.title: Napari Viewer controls
docs.text:
For this plugin the Points Layer is the most common and important type of layer, so it may be useful to read napari's documentation on that. The most important controls will be shown on this page.

  1. Napari Terminal: Open the Napari integrated terminal.
  2. 3-D viewer: Toggle 3-D view, essential for navigating 3-D/4D datasets (Ctrl+Y).
  3. Grid view: The grid view will place datasets in different views that are still controlled with the same controls, it is only important if multiple datasets are shown simultaneously on viewer, which overlap (Ctrl+G).
  4. Napari Viewer: The datasets imported will be shown on this viewer, and its visualization and navigation capabilities are harnessed throughout the whole plugin. Some important buttons:
    • Drag Left Click: Rotate the dataset.
    • Shift Left Click: Move the dataset.
    • Scroll: Zoom in and out.
    • Shift Right Click: Select one node. When a node is selected the Lineage Viewer will also show the corresponding lineage on the Lineage Viewer.

Using the time slider on the Napari Viewer will also show the corresponding timepoint, as a grey line, on the Lineage Viewer.
